subtype: Approach: dismissing it as attention seeking [Pitfall]
passage:
“I don't think anyone would even notice if I stopped coming,” Lalremsiami said, eyes on the cracked tiles of the bus stop.
“Oh come on, you say this every exam week.”
“No, I mean it this time. I can't sleep and I don't want to eat.”
“You're exaggerating, Lali. Seriously. Did you finish the maths sheet?”
“Uma, I—”
“The bus is so late. Did you see what Nisha posted?”
Uma told herself it was only a bid for attention from her friend, and that if it were real, Lalremsiami would have said it differently. Lalremsiami looked at her, nodded slowly and pulled her scarf higher. The counsellor's room was two floors above them, and neither mentioned it. On the bus they sat side by side without a word, and Lalremsiami got off two stops early.

qa.q: Where were Uma and Lalremsiami when they talked?
qa.a: They were at the bus stop, and the counsellor's room was two floors above them.

qa.q: What was Uma thinking when she changed the subject?
qa.a: Uma thought it was only a bid for attention, and she probably felt uncomfortable, so she turned to the maths sheet and the late bus.

qa.q: What could Uma try instead, and why?
qa.a: Uma could ask what Lalremsiami means, listen, and offer to walk with her to the counsellor upstairs, because not sleeping, not eating and saying nobody would notice deserve to be taken seriously.

qa.q: How did Lalremsiami likely feel after the talk?
qa.a: More alone: she pulled her scarf higher, stayed silent on the bus and got off two stops early.

grounding: A teen tells herself her friend is exaggerating and changes the subject, missing the chance to link her with help.
